title: Sambhar Daal
description: A tangy and spicy South Indian lentil stew made with toor dal, mixed vegetables, and a fragrant tamarind-based broth. Perfect with idli, dosa, or steamed rice.
ingredients: 2 cups mixed vegetables (drumstick, eggplant, tomato, pearl onions, carrot)
1 small lemon-sized ball of tamarind (soaked in 1/2 cup warm water)
instructions: Wash the toor dal and pressure cook with turmeric, a pinch of salt, and 2.5 cups water for 3–4 whistles until soft. Mash well and set aside.
Soak tamarind in warm water for 10 minutes, then extract the juice and discard the pulp.
In a pot, add the tamarind water, chopped tomatoes, mixed vegetables, sambhar powder, and salt. Bring to a boil and cook until vegetables are tender (about 10–12 minutes).
Add the mashed toor dal to the pot and stir well. Simmer for 5 minutes, adjusting consistency with water if needed.
For the tempering: heat oil or ghee in a small pan. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter, then add cumin seeds, dried red chilies, curry leaves, and asafoetida. Sauté for 30 seconds.
Pour the tempering over the sambhar and stir to combine.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve hot with idli, dosa, or steamed rice.
notes: For best flavour, use homemade sambhar powder. Drumstick (moringa) is a traditional favourite — add it along with the other vegetables. Sambhar thickens as it sits; thin it out with a little water when reheating.
